title: Understand what a product manager does
summary: A product manager makes sure the team builds the right thing: something users need, that works for the organisation and that can be built. Knowing what the role is, and is not, helps you focus your time.

beginner: Learn the four risks every PM manages: will people want it, can they use it, can we build it, and does it work for the business.
Write down the outcomes you are responsible for, not just the tasks you do.
Find out how your organisation divides work between you, design, engineering, delivery and any product owner.
Book short one-to-ones with each role in your team and ask what they need from you.
Each week, check how much of your time went on users, the team and stakeholders. Aim for a balance.
Pick one experienced PM to learn from and meet them regularly.
intermediate: Map your responsibilities against value, usability, feasibility and viability.
Agree role boundaries with your team.
Review where your time goes each month.
experienced: Coach new PMs on the role and on outcomes over output.
Help your organisation define product roles clearly.
Model the role through your own habits.

canDelegateTo.task: Explain how delivery and product work together here

toolExamples.notion: Keep a simple weekly log of where your time went and what you learned.
toolExamples.claude: Describe your week and ask which activities moved outcomes and which did not.

definitionOfDone: Role boundaries agreed with your team
A mentor or peer to learn from
pitfalls: Becoming the team's note-taker or ticket-writer only
Trying to be the designer or engineer as well
